consoleIssues.message: Uncaught Error: Minified React error #418 (hydration mismatch: 'Hydration failed because the initial UI does not match what was rendered on the server')
consoleIssues.observedOn: first navigation to /verify-email?email=test%40example.com in this session
consoleIssues.likelyRootCause: verify-email-form.tsx `getRestoredCountdown()` reads `sessionStorage` synchronously inside `useState(() => ...)` initializer. Server-side render always sees no sessionStorage (returns 0 → renders resend-button branch), while the client's first paint can read a pre-existing `verify-email-countdown-start` value from a prior visit in the same tab/session and render the '{seconds}s' countdown branch instead — a classic SSR/CSR branch mismatch. Intermittent: only reproduces when sessionStorage already holds a non-expired countdown from an earlier visit; a clean reload without prior storage does not trigger it.
consoleIssues.recommendation: Guard the countdown-restore branch so the first client render matches SSR (e.g. always initialize to 0 and correct via useEffect after mount), or wrap in useSyncExternalStore/suppressHydrationWarning if intentional.

networkObservations.observation: Every plain navigation/reload of /verify-email?email=... (i.e. without &sent=1) fires a fresh POST /api/auth/email-otp/send-verification-otp on mount (verify-email-form.tsx useEffect `if (sent) return; emailOtp.sendVerificationOtp(...)`), and the backend returned {success:true} again ~15s after the prior send — well inside the client-displayed 60s resend cooldown.
networkObservations.impact: A user (or anyone with the verify-email URL + email query param) can trigger repeated verification-code emails simply by refreshing the page, bypassing the cooldown UX shown on screen (and the backend did not appear to rate-limit the rapid repeat request either in this smoke check). Potential for email spam / notification abuse against arbitrary addresses since the endpoint does not appear to validate the email belongs to a real pending session before returning success.
networkObservations.recommendation: Have the effect check the restored countdown (or a server-verified cooldown) before calling sendVerificationOtp, and confirm backend-side rate limiting on this endpoint independent of the client UI.

networkObservations.observation: POST /api/auth/email-otp/send-verification-otp returned 200 {success:true} for the placeholder address test@example.com (no real pending verification), i.e. no visible error state was shown to the user — countdown started normally as if a real email had been sent.
networkObservations.recommendation: Confirm this is intentional (anti user-enumeration behavior) rather than a missing validation error.
